                           UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
                        FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                                ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


 MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

                Plaintiff,

                V.                                               Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
                                                                 The Honorable Judge
                                                                 Rossie D. Alston Jr.
 KATIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
                Defendants.

 MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF'S RULE 72(a) OBJECTIONS TO ECF
      NO. 96 AND MOTION TO SET ASIDE OR MODIFY THAT ORDER, DETERMINE
      REASSIGNMENT AUTHORITY, AND GRANT LEAVE TO SUPPLEMENT ECF NO.
                                                   93


 I.      PRELIMINARY STATEMENT
         The October 22, 2026 docket records reassignment of this action to Magistrate Judge

 Fitzpatrick and states that Magistrate Judge Davis is no longer assigned. ECF No. 96, signed by

 Magistrate Judge Davis, disposes of Plaintiff's disqualification motion on the ground that the case

 has been reassigned. The quotations from ECF No. 96 in this Memorandum are taken from its

 October 22, 2026 docket entry. Plaintiff objects to that adjudication to the extent it occurred after

 the authority necessary to decide ECF No. 86 had ended or exceeded the administrative action

 permissible after recusal or statutory disqualification.

         The available record does not establish the effective scope of the reassignment, whether

 authority over ECF No. 86 remained, or the procedure used to designate the successor. Plaintiff




                                                   1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 99      Filed 10/23/26     Page 2 of 16 PageID#
                                              1007



 requests determination of those matters and vacatur if the challenged disposition lacked authority

 or constituted prohibited participation.

        Independently, Plaintiff requests that the District Judge determine the October 22

 developments' effect on pending ECF No. 93. At minimum, the completed prospective

 reassignment must remain distinct from the unresolved requests concerning ECF Nos. 64 and 84.

 ECF No. 96 does not determine the financial-conflict facts or the retrospective application.

 Plaintiff requests adjudication of that application on its own grounds, with factual determinations

 to the extent necessary, and without delaying independently warranted relief on the existing

 objections.

 II.    PROCEDURAL HISTORY AND GOVERNING REVIEW
        A.       Chronology
        On September 9, 2026, ECF No. 64 required Plaintiff to file by September 11, 2026 a

 redlined comparison of the proposed Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint (ECF No.

 59-1) against the original Complaint (ECF No. 1). On September 13, 2026, Plaintiff submitted

 Rule 72(a) objections to ECF Nos. 63, 64, and 65 and a motion to set aside ECF No. 64 (ECF Nos.

 66, 67, 68). On October 7, 2026, ECF No. 84 denied ECF Nos. 15 and 54 as premature and denied

 ECF No. 59 for nonproduction of the comparison.

        On October 13, 2026, Plaintiff filed three coordinated applications, each entered October

 14, 2026. ECF No. 86 moved before Magistrate Judge Davis for disqualification under 28 U.S.C.

 § 455(b)(4) and § 455(a), supported by a Declaration and by Exhibits A and B, the Financial

 Disclosure Reports for calendar years 2025 and 2024 (ECF Nos. 86-1 through 86-3). ECF Nos.

 89, 90, and 91 presented Rule 72(a) objections to ECF No. 84 before the District Judge. ECF Nos.

 93 and 94 moved before the District Judge for targeted vacatur of ECF Nos. 64 and 84, withdrawal

 or modification of the referral, and interim relief.



                                                    2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 99         Filed 10/23/26      Page 3 of 16 PageID#
                                             1008



        On October 22, 2026, the docket recorded the reassignment of this action to Magistrate

 Judge Fitzpatrick and the entry of ECF No. 96. Both actions are dated October 22, 2026. ECF No.

 96 describes the reassignment as completed. The available entries do not establish the relative

 timing of execution, issuance, entry, and the effective termination or modification of the relevant

 designation.

        B.      The allocation of issues among the October 13 filings
        ECF No. 86 asked the Magistrate Judge to state on the record whether the asset reported as

 "FB common stock" is common stock of Meta Platforms, Inc.; whether that interest was held on

 July 30, 2026 and on each date on which ECF Nos. 62, 63, 64, 65, 82, and 84 were entered; the

 date and manner of any divestiture; whether the interest is held directly or through a fund within

 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4)(i); and any other fact material to§ 455(f). ECF No. 86, Part V. It requested

 disqualification upon those determinations and, upon disqualification, "the ministerial steps

 necessary to return or transfer the referred matters through the Court's assignment procedures." Id.,

 Parts V, VII{Al)-(A4). It stated that the companion filings "seek the retrospective and case-

 management remedies" and that "[t]his Motion does not." Id., Part VI. It reserved review under

 Rule 72(a) of any order disposing of it. Id.

        ECF No. 93 requests the retrospective and referral relief. ECF No. 93 ,i 10 states seven

 requests: {Rl) withdrawal or modification of the referral, with affected matters retained by the

 District Judge or reassigned through the Court's assignment procedures; (R2) vacatur of ECF No.

 84 and of the comparison requirement and deadline in ECF No. 64 upon the statutory findings

 identified in its paragraph 5; (R3) restoration of ECF Nos. 15, 54, and 59 to pending status; (R4)

 affirmative adjudication of those motions or prompt independent determination; (RS) interim

 protection; (R6) coordinated determination with the existing objections; and (R7) a decision

 record. ECF No. 93 ,i 2 states that it does not extend or restart any period to object.


                                                   3

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 99         Filed 10/23/26      Page 4 of 16 PageID#
                                             1009



        C.      ECF No. 96
        The docket entry for ECF No. 96 identifies ECF No. 86 as the matter before the Court,

 states that the matter "can be resolved without oral argument," orders that the Motion "is DENIED

 AS MOOT," and states: "The case has been reassigned to Magistrate Judge William E.

 Fitzpatrick." The entry records no determination on any item in ECF No. 86, Part V. It does not

 refer to ECF No. 93. It does not identify the basis for the reassignment or the authority under which

 ECF No. 96 was entered after the reassignment it describes.

        D.      Governing review
        The district judge "must consider timely objections and modify or set aside any part of the

 order that is clearly erroneous or is contrary to law." Fed. R. Civ. P. 72(a); 28 U.S.C. § 636(b){l)

 (A). Whether a magistrate judge possessed authority to decide a matter is a question of law. A

 disposition entered without that authority is contrary to law. Plaintiff does not seek de novo

 reconsideration under Rule 72(b). Wall v. Rasnick, 42 F.4th 214 (4th Cir. 2022) (No. 21-6553, slip

 op. at 3), states the Rule 72(a) framework. It does not decide when a reassignment terminates a

 magistrate judge's authority, and Plaintiff does not cite it for that proposition.

        A district judge "may designate a magistrate judge to hear and determine any pretrial matter

 pending before the court," subject to the exceptions stated in § 636(b){l){A). In this District,

 "[m]agistrate judges . . . are authorized and specially designated to perform all duties authorized

 or allowed to be performed by United States magistrate judges by the United States Code and any

 rule governing proceedings in this Court," and "[d]uties and cases may be assigned or referred to

 a magistrate judge by an order entered in the action or on the instructions of a district judge." E.D.

 Va. Loe. Civ. R. 72. The same rule provides that a Rule 72(a) objection "shall be considered a

 motion and is subject to the briefing and notice requirements on Local Civil Rule 7." Id. The

 District Judge controls the scope of the referral. The present record concerns an ordinary pretrial



                                                   4

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 99        Filed 10/23/26      Page 5 of 16 PageID#
                                             1010



 referral, and Plaintiff does not invoke the standard for vacating a consensual reference under §

 636(c)(4).

        ECF No. 93 invokes Rule 54(b) for revision of ECF Nos. 64 and 84. Plaintiff maintains

 that authority there. Plaintiff does not invoke Rule 60(b )( 4) and does not contend that any order is

 void. Timely objection under Rule 72(a) is the vehicle for review of ECF No. 96.

 III.   AUTHORITY TO ISSUE ECF NO. 96
        A.      The issue
        Magistrate Judge Davis remained a magistrate judge of this District on October 22, 2026.

 The question is whether, when ECF No. 96 was issued, he retained authority to adjudicate ECF

 No. 86 in this action.

        Plaintiff objects to the disposition of ECF No. 86 if, when ECF No. 96 was issued, the

 reassignment had terminated the authority necessary to adjudicate that motion and no applicable

 statutory, standing, or case-specific authority permitted the disposition. Plaintiff requests

 identification of the operative authority and the effect of reassignment on it. The objection does

 not rest merely on the absence of a separately docketed referral order.

        B.      What the record does and does not establish
        ECF No. 96 gives one reason for its disposition: the case "has been reassigned." The

 reassignment entry states that Magistrate Judge Davis is "no longer assigned to the case." The two

 entries together describe a completed reassignment and a disposition that relies on it. They do not

 establish the relative timing of execution, issuance, entry, and the effective termination or

 modification of the designation. They do not state whether the reassignment withdrew every matter

 then pending before Magistrate Judge Davis in this action or preserved any specified matter.

        Plaintiff does not assert that the reassignment entry terminated every possible source of

 authority. Plaintiff does not assume that a motion under advisement remained with Magistrate



                                                   5

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 99        Filed 10/23/26       Page 6 of 16 PageID#
                                              1011



 Judge Davis. Those are competing propositions. The docket does not resolve them. Local Civil

 Rule 72 permits referral "on the instructions of a district judge" without an entered order, and an

 instruction of that kind would not appear on the docket. For that reason the objection asks the

 Court to identify the operative authority, in whatever form it took, and to determine whether the

 disposition of ECF No. 86 fell within it.

         C.     The record request
         Plaintiff requests that the District Judge place on the record, in the decision itself, through

 a statement of the Clerk, or from existing records, four matters:

         1.      The effective scope of the reassignment and, where material and available, its

 timing relative to ECF No. 96.

         2.      Whether authority over ECF No. 86 remained and the source of that authority.

         3.      Whether     the   reassignment      reflected   recusal,    another    disqualification

 determination, or another administrative basis relevant to the Objections.

         4.      The governing successor-selection procedure and whether that procedure was

 followed.

         Plaintiff requests an opportunity to address any newly supplied material factual information

 before it becomes a basis for decision. Plaintiff does not request a deposition of any judicial officer,

 access to chambers communications, inquiry into judicial mental processes, or the production of

 timestamps that may not exist. The request is for the source of administrative authority, which the

 Court can state.




                                                    6

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 99         Filed 10/23/26      Page 7 of 16 PageID#
                                             1012



 IV.    RECUSAL,         STATUTORY           DISQUALIFICATION,              AND      PERMISSIBLE
        ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION
        A.      Three distinct circumstances
        The second objection is independent of the first. It requires the Court to distinguish three

 circumstances. The first is an established recusal. The second is an established statutory duty to

 disqualify under 28 U.S.C. § 455. The third is the mere pendency of a motion requesting

 disqualification. The filing of a § 455 motion does not establish the alleged financial interest. It

 does not eliminate the judge's ability to decide the motion. The statutory conditions in § 455(b)

 (4), § 455( d)( 4), and § 455(f) must be addressed before a duty to disqualify is established. The

 issue under this objection is whether ECF No. 96 was an authorized administrative disposition or

 prohibited adjudication under the circumstances the Court determines to exist.

        B.      Participation after recusal
        In Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC v. NTE Carolinas II, LLC, No. 22-2168, slip op. at 52-54

 (4th Cir. Aug. 5, 2024) (published), reported at 111 F.4th 337, a district judge recused under a

 prophylactic policy, the Clerk reassigned the case and recorded "conflict" as the reason, and the

 case later returned to the same judge. The Fourth Circuit held that once a judge recuses himself

 from a case he should remain recused, even though the recusal may not originally have been

 required. Id. at 4, 52-54. The court relied on Arnold v. Eastern Air Lines, Inc., 712 F.2d 899, 904-

 05 (4th Cir. 1983) (en bane), for the rule that a recused judge is "out of service insofar as that case

 is concerned" and "should take no action which would possibly affect the outcome of [the] case."

 Duke Energy, slip op. at 53 (quoting Arnold, 712 F .2d at 904-05).

        Duke Energy supports the rule against a recused judge acting in the same case. It does not

 hold that every same-day reassignment and docket-closing order is invalid. Its facts involved a

 clerk-recorded reassignment based on a conflict, which shows that the absence of a document




                                                   7

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 99        Filed 10/23/26         Page 8 of 16 PageID#
                                             1013



 labeled "recusal" is not dispositive of whether a recusal occurred. Timing alone does not establish

 that the reassignment here was a recusal. The record does not say what it was. That is the third

 matter in the record request.

         C.     Permissible administrative action
         In re BellSouth Corp., 334 F.3d 941, 949-50 & n.4 (11th Cir. 2003), distinguishes

 substantive participation from administrative transfer. The district judge there did not rule on the

 merits and did not designate a successor. He referred the matter to the Clerk for random

 reassignment and stayed the matters before him. The Eleventh Circuit held that the referral was

 ministerial and contrasted cases in which a judge continued to enter substantive orders after the

 duty to recuse arose. Id. at 949-50. The court also recognized that technical error of this kind does

 not invariably warrant vacatur, and it applied the Liljeberg factors in that assessment. Id. at 949

 n.4. BellSouth arose on a petition for mandamus. Its mandamus standard does not govern this Rule

 72(a) application. Its distinction between substantive participation and administrative transfer

 does.

         McCuin v. Texas Power & Light Co., 714 F.2d 1255, 1261 (5th Cir. 1983), holds that a

 disqualified judge "has no authority to sign such an order, or any other judicial order, pertaining

 to a proceeding in which he is disqualified." The Fifth Circuit vacated the disqualified judge's

 order assigning the cases to a named successor. Id.

         Plaintiff contends that disposing of ECF No. 86 after the relevant authority ended would

 exceed implementation of a transfer. The Court should determine whether ECF No. 96 was

 authorized adjudication, permissible administrative closure, or action beyond the authority

 remaining. Its title and dispositive verb do not alone resolve that question.




                                                   8

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 99        Filed 10/23/26      Page 9 of 16 PageID#
                                            1014



        D.      Plaintiff's prior request
        ECF No. 86 requested determination of the statutory question and supporting facts before

 further substantive action, followed, upon disqualification, by transfer through the Court's

 procedures. ECF No. 86, Part VII(A3)-(A4). Plaintiff does not object merely because Judge Davis

 addressed a motion directed to him. The present objection concerns the authority and permissible

 scope of the disposition in light of the completed reassignment described in ECF No. 96.

        E.      The statutory grounds are maintained
        The record on which ECF No. 86 rests remains before the Court. The Financial Disclosure

 Reports for calendar years 2025 and 2024 report "FB common stock" at Part VII, line 6, with a

 gross year-end value of $15,001 to $50,000 and no reported transaction on that line. ECF No. 86-

 2 at 2; ECF No. 86-3 at 4. The public filings establishing the relationship between "FB" and Meta

 Platforms, Inc. are identified in ECF No. 87, Part II.B. Section 455(b)(4) requires disqualification

 where the judge knows that he has a financial interest in a party. Section 455(d)(4) defines a

 financial interest as ownership of a legal or equitable interest "however small," with the exception

 in§ 455(d)(4)(i) for an interest held through a mutual or common investment fund. Section 455(f)

 permits divestiture to cure a disqualification discovered after substantial judicial time has been

 devoted to the matter. Section 455(a) applies independently.

        The reports establish the holding at year-end 2024 and year-end 2025. They do not establish

 the holding on any date in 2026. ECF No. 86, Part II; ECF No. 93 , 5. ECF No. 96 did not

 determine the factual questions identified in ECF No. 86, Part V. Those questions remain relevant

 to the extent necessary to decide the statutory grounds and retrospective relief presented in ECF

 No. 93. Plaintiff requests that the District Judge address them in that proceeding rather than treat

 the completed reassignment as resolving them. A mootness disposition supplies no finding on

 ownership, knowledge, divestiture, or statutory compliance. The inclusion of requested findings



                                                  9

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 99        Filed 10/23/26    Page 10 of 16 PageID#
                                             1015



 in ECF No. 86 does not by itself require the Court to make every finding after the prospective

 request has become unnecessary. Fed. R. Civ. P. 52(a)(3). Plaintiff requests a factual and legal

 basis sufficient to decide the relief still sought, and no more.

 V.      SUCCESSOR DESIGNATION AND CONDITIONAL CORRECTION
        A disqualified judge may not select the judge who will succeed to the case. McCuin, 714

 F.2d at 1261. Permitting that selection "would violate the congressional command that the

 disqualified judge be removed from all participation in the case" and "might, in addition, create

 suspicion that the disqualified judge will select a successor whose views are consonant with his."

 Id. Referral to the Clerk for assignment under the court's procedures is permitted. BellSouth, 334

 F.3d at 949-50. The application of McCuin depends on facts not established here. The record does

 not identify who directed the reassignment or under what procedure, and the absence of a publicly

 described selection mechanism is not proof that the selection was unauthorized.

         Plaintiff requests identification of the authority and procedure that produced the successor

 designation. If the designation resulted from discretionary selection by a disqualified officer or

 another unauthorized process, Plaintiff requests correction under the Court's governing

 assignment procedures, administered without the disqualified officer's participation. Plaintiff

 requests Clerk-administered random selection to the extent authorized by those procedures. If the

 existing designation complied with the governing procedure, Plaintiff requests that determination.

        This request bears on the first objection and on the pending referral relief in ECF No. 93 ,i

 lO(Rl). If the officer who issued ECF No. 96 also directed the successor designation, the authority

 for both acts rests on the same determination. ECF No. 93 ,i lO(Rl) requests that affected matters

 be reassigned "through the Court's assignment procedures." Identification of the procedure

 actually used answers whether that request has been satisfied.




                                                   10

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 99         Filed 10/23/26       Page 11 of 16 PageID#
                                             1016



          Plaintiff claims no right to a different magistrate judge. A procedure conducted under the

 Court's rules may designate Magistrate Judge Fitzpatrick. Plaintiff raises no objection to

 Magistrate Judge Fitzpatrick personally and does not seek the reinstatement of Magistrate Judge

 Davis.

 VI.      ECF NO. 96'S EFFECT ON PENDING ECF NO. 93; ALTERNATIVE RELIEF
          ECF No. 96 disposed of ECF No. 86 on mootness grounds following reassignment. It did

 not determine whether the challenged earlier participation complied with § 455 and did not

 adjudicate ECF No. 93. Plaintiff requests that the District Judge decide ECF No. 93 on its own

 grounds, resolving the statutory facts to the extent necessary to that decision, or granting

 independently warranted relief without reaching unnecessary questions.

          Plaintiff does not contend that ECF No. 96 purports to decide ECF No. 93, and Plaintiff

 does not ask the Court to restore every determination requested in ECF No. 86 as a standalone

 controversy. The live relief is the requested correction of ECF Nos. 64 and 84 and the pending

 referral questions. The determinations necessary to that relief belong in the District Judge's

 resolution of the pending applications, on an appropriate factual record. Plaintiff does not request

 that any inquiry be returned to Magistrate Judge Davis.

          Liljeberg v. Health Services Acquisition Corp., 486 U.S. 847, 862-64 (1988), separates the

 question whether a judge should have disqualified himself from the question what remedy follows

 for past participation. The Court identified three considerations for the remedial question: the risk

 of injustice to the parties in the particular case, the risk that denial of relief will produce injustice

 in other cases, and the risk of undermining the public's confidence in the judicial process. Id. at

 864. Liljeberg arose on a Rule 60(b )(6) motion for relief from a final judgment. The present

 application concerns interlocutory orders, and the grounds invoked in ECF No. 93, including Rule

 54(b) and§ 636(b){l){A), supply the vehicle. Vacatur does not follow automatically from a§ 455


                                                    11

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 99         Filed 10/23/26      Page 12 of 16 PageID#
                                            1017



 violation. The remedial question, where reached, is decided on the Liljeberg considerations and on

 the record the Court develops.

         The District Judge may grant complete relief from ECF Nos. 64 and 84 on the procedural

 grounds independently briefed in ECF Nos. 66, 67, 89, 90, and 91 without deciding every financial-

 conflict question. Plaintiff preserves that route and does not make any collateral determination a

 prerequisite to it.

 VII.    CONSEQUENCES, COORDINATED DETERMINATION, AND LEAVE TO
         SUPPLEMENT
         A.       Consequences
         The consequence of any defect in ECF No. 96 must be assessed separately from the

 continuing effects of ECF Nos. 64 and 84. An authorized district-judge determination that

 considers the preserved grounds and supplies appropriate relief may eliminate any remaining

 consequence of the October 22 disposition. Reassignment alone does not perform that review.

 Rule 61 directs the Court to disregard errors that do not affect a party's substantial rights, and

 Plaintiff requests correction matched to the consequence established, not reversal for its own sake.

 Fed. R. Civ. P. 61.

         Leaving necessary issues unresolved while the challenged orders control the operative

 pleading can matter on review. In Wall v. Rasnick, 42 F.4th 214 (4th Cir. 2022) (No. 21-6553, slip

 op. at 3, 9-10), timely and specific Rule 72(a) objections remained reviewable when the final

 judgment implicitly rejected them, and the court vacated because the underlying issues had been

 left unresolved by the magistrate judge and were material to the result. Plaintiff does not contend

 that every omitted finding, unexplained ruling, or implicit denial is reversible. Plaintiff states the

 issues here with the specificity that Rule 72(a) and Rule 46 require so that the Court can decide

 them.



                                                  12

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 99        Filed 10/23/26      Page 13 of 16 PageID#
                                            1018



        Plaintiff maintains by reference the requests concerning ECF No. 64 (ECF Nos. 66, 67;

 ECF No.93110(R2)), ECF No. 84 (ECF Nos. 89, 90, 91; ECF No.93110(R2)-(R4)), and ECF

 No. 59 (ECF No.93110(R3)-(R4)). This Memorandum does not repeat their merits. This package

 does not restart any period to object.

        B.      Coordinated determination
        Plaintiff requests that the District Judge retain determination of the authority and

 assignment questions and coordinate them with ECF No. 93 and the pending objections. ECF No.

 931 10(R6). Plaintiff maintains the request in ECF No. 931 l0(RS)(c) that the amendment and

 financial-conflict issues be determined before, or expressly within, any disposition of ECF Nos.

 10, 21, or 45 that would terminate a claim and that relies on the exclusion of the proposed pleading.

 Plaintiff does not request a stay. The pendency of these Objections does not prevent the Court from

 granting independently warranted relief on the amendment and discovery objections, and Plaintiff

 requests that relief without awaiting resolution of every assignment question. ECF No. 93 1

 10(R6).

        C.      Leave to supplement
        Local Civil Rule ?(F)(l) provides that "[n]o further briefs or written communications may

 be filed without first obtaining leave of Court." The October 22 developments postdate ECF No.

 93 and bear on its requests (Rl), (RS), and (R6). The Proposed Supplement, Exhibit A, is confined

 to those developments and their effect on ECF No.93110. It repeats no argument from ECF No.

 94 and adds no ground. Plaintiff requests leave to file it, with such opportunity for the Defendants

 to respond as the Court directs. Rule 15(d) governs supplemental pleadings and is not invoked.

 VIII. CONCLUSION
        Plaintiff requests that the Court (1) grant leave to file Exhibit A; (2) retain determination

 of the Objections and place on the record the four matters identified in Part 111.C; (3) determine



                                                  13

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF           Document 99       Filed 10/23/26      Page 14 of 16 PageID#
                                           1019



 Objections One and Two and, if either is sustained, vacate ECF No. 96 and dispose independently

 of ECF No. 86's prospective request; (4) in the alternative, define the limited effect of ECF No.

 96 and determine ECF No. 93 on its own grounds; (5) identify the authority and procedure that

 produced the successor designation and correct it if it was unauthorized; and (6) coordinate these

 determinations with the pending applications, distinguishing relief granted, requests pending, and

 requests rendered unnecessary.
